title: Why Can't You Ever Reach a Rainbow?
pause_note: 'long' lists beat indices followed by a pause; Short: 0.6 s

beats: Why can't you ever reach a rainbow?
Walk toward one, and it backs away. Step sideways, and it follows you.
That's because a rainbow isn't a thing in the sky. It's an angle.
Some sunlight enters a raindrop, bends, bounces off the back, and comes out again.
It comes back out bunched up about forty-two degrees from the path the sunlight came in on.
Each colour bends a little differently, so red and violet come out at slightly different angles.
So the bow is made by drops about forty-two degrees from the shadow of your head, as seen from your eye.
Take a step, and a different set of drops lights up. The bow moves with you.
You can't reach it, because it's always forty-two degrees away.
